analysis:
The supplied changes are tests only: scripts/test-provider-release-pipeline.py (head lines ~450-645) and scripts/test-provider-release-publication.py (new ClusterRuntimeTests at head ~308-659). No production code is changed in this batch, so no direct regression in provider-side controls is visible.

What the tests pin (which the next pass should check against the real implementation, not in the supplied evidence): (1) The release workflow computes cluster-runtime facts from the final signed app. The facts step references no secrets, runs the app CLI under `env -i`, and deletes the signing keychain and the secret-derived GITHUB_ENV values before any release code runs. It also verifies the bundle hash before extraction. The tests assert these ordering properties. (2) The cluster_runtime block is sent to the coordinator only when the per-environment `*_CLUSTER_RUNTIME_ENABLED` variable is true and publish is true. Otherwise the payload is byte-identical to the old one, pinned by SHA-256. (3) The publication helper strictly validates the block: canonical JSON, duplicate-key rejection, 64 KiB bound, 64 models, derived-ID length limits, a registration-body limit, zero/uppercase digest refusal, and only `prepare` accepting the block. (4) The qualification sharding tests assert a single audited gate job (`Qualify provider with SDK 27`) with `needs` on the shards, no secrets, and no always()/continue-on-error, so signing is still gated by a complete qualification audit.

Relevant threats: T-054 (unqualified build accepted), T-053, T-034 (build/identity binding), and A-017 (durable qualifications). The block carries pair_serving_grant and parity_qualifications evidence. The coordinator's treatment of these fields as authoritative versus advisory is platform-owned and outside the supplied evidence. The next pass should confirm the coordinator does not treat the block as a serving authorization without independent evidence. That is a question for the next pass, not a finding.

The tests are weaker than a running workflow because they assert source-text properties only. I could not see the actual workflow, facts script or publication script, so coverage of those is limited.
